issues.legal_issue: When mortgaged land is let to a tenant, redemption of the mortgage does not make the owners Bhumidhars of the area occupied by the tenant.
material_facts: The owners had mortgaged the land in possession of a mortgagee.
Before the relevant land-reform law commenced, the mortgagee let the land to a tenant, who sublet it to a person who was in possession when the law commenced.
The owners later applied to redeem the mortgage, and the land was subsequently acquired for a public purpose.
issues.conclusion: The owners could not become Bhumidhars of the area occupied by the tenant; the tenant was entitled to Bhumidhar status for that area and to the Bhumidhar's portion of the compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 15(2) and 15(4) of the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954, an owner redeeming a mortgage could be declared a Bhumidhar only for the mortgaged area under the mortgagee's personal cultivation, while tenants were to be declared Bhumidhars for areas let to them. Sections 13(1) and 13(2) provided for acquisition of Bhumidhar rights by eligible tenants. In the compensation reference treated under section 32 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the person holding those rights was entitled to the Bhumidhar's portion of the compensation. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: mortgage_redemption_case and land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding and mortgaged_land_was_let_to_tenant and tenant_or_subtenant_possessed_land and tenant_qualified_for_bhumidhar_status

predicates.mortgage_redemption_case: The dispute concerns owners who sought to redeem land that had been mortgaged.
predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The dispute arose in a proceeding to determine entitlement to compensation for acquired land.
predicates.mortgaged_land_was_let_to_tenant: The mortgagee had let the mortgaged land to a tenant.
predicates.tenant_or_subtenant_possessed_land: A tenant or subtenant was in possession of the land when the relevant land-reform law commenced.
predicates.tenant_qualified_for_bhumidhar_status: The person in possession belonged to a class of tenant entitled to acquire Bhumidhar status.

issues.definition: If a mortgage-redemption dispute in a land-acquisition compensation proceeding concerns land let to a qualifying tenant or subtenant in possession, the tenant is entitled to Bhumidhar status and compensation.

issues.legal_issue: An eligible tenant acquires Bhumidhar rights by operation of law even if the required administrative declaration is delayed or never made.
material_facts: The person claiming compensation was in possession as a subtenant when the land-reform law commenced.
The person was eligible to acquire Bhumidhar rights under the law.
The administrative declaration of Bhumidhar status was made later, and the owners argued that their redemption of the mortgage made them entitled to the compensation instead.
issues.conclusion: The delay in, or absence of, a declaration did not prevent the eligible tenant from acquiring Bhumidhar rights from the date those rights arose under the law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1) of the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954 required the Deputy Commissioner to declare eligible classes of tenants as Bhumidhars with effect from commencement of the Act. Section 13(2) gave a person acquiring Bhumidhar rights the rights and liabilities of a Bhumidhar from the date of acquisition. Sections 15(2) and 15(4) likewise imposed an obligation to declare persons who had become entitled to that status. The declaration was therefore not a prerequisite to the acquisition of rights. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding and tenant_status_dispute and tenant_was_eligible_for_statutory_status and declaration_was_delayed_or_absent

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The dispute arose in a proceeding to determine entitlement to compensation for acquired land.
predicates.tenant_status_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a person occupying land as a tenant acquired statutory landholder status.
predicates.tenant_was_eligible_for_statutory_status: The person was within a class of tenant entitled under the law to acquire the status.
predicates.declaration_was_delayed_or_absent: The required administrative declaration was made only after a delay or was not made.

issues.definition: If an eligible tenant's status is disputed in a compensation proceeding and the declaration is delayed or absent, the tenant's status arises when the statutory entitlement arises.

issues.legal_issue: An admission between other claimants about who received compensation does not bind the person claiming that compensation.
material_facts: Two claimants asserted that a partition had allotted the relevant land to them and that they alone had received the compensation.
They asked that, if the appeals failed, only they be required to pay the compensation to the person claiming entitlement to it.
That person's entitlement was being determined in the appeal, and the admission was made between other claimants.
issues.conclusion: The admission could not bind the person claiming the compensation, so the request to limit responsibility to the two recipients was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: An admission between other claimants about their partition and receipt of compensation does not bind a claimant who was not bound by that arrangement. The Court relied on no statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.compensation_entitlement_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning entitlement to land-acquisition compensation.
predicates.other_claimants_admit_receiving_compensa: Other claimants admit that they received the compensation under an allocation made between them.
predicates.claimant_is_not_bound_by_that_allocation: The person claiming the compensation was not bound by the private allocation or its related admission.

issues.definition: If other claimants in a compensation appeal rely on a private allocation and admission that do not bind the claimant, that admission does not bind the claimant.
